questions.q: In a standard generator set, which specific component is responsible for regulating the voltage output to ensure it stays within safe operating limits?
questions.n: This component automatically maintains a constant voltage level, protecting connected equipment from fluctuations.

questions.q: Which of the following conduit types is the only one permitted by the Philippine Electrical Code (PEC) for use in electrical service entrances due to its high physical strength?
questions.n: RSC is a heavy-duty, threaded metallic tubing that provides maximum protection against mechanical damage.

questions.q: What is the standard nominal voltage and frequency typically supplied to residential and commercial buildings in the Philippines?
questions.n: The Philippines follows the 230V standard at a frequency of 60 Hertz for its power grid.

questions.q: If you need to control a single light fixture from four different locations, what specific combination of switches must be installed?
questions.n: The two 3-way switches act as terminal controls, while the two 4-way switches allow for intermediate control points.

questions.q: What is the primary technical reason why telephone (data) wires and electrical (power) wires should not be placed in the same conduit or close together?
o: The wires might melt into each other
It is too expensive to install together
questions.n: The magnetic field from power lines can induce noise and crosstalk in data lines, leading to data corruption.

questions.q: Which system is specifically designed to provide instantaneous battery power to critical electronics the moment a power outage occurs, bridging the gap until a generator starts?
questions.n: A UPS uses internal batteries to maintain power without a single millisecond of interruption.

questions.q: In an office with a high density of computers and networking equipment, which architectural floor system is most appropriate for managing extensive cabling?
questions.n: The space beneath the modular tiles allows for massive cable runs and easy access for technical changes.

questions.q: What does the abbreviation 'PABX' stand for in the context of office communication systems?
questions.n: A PABX is a private telephone network used within a company to manage multiple internal and external calls.

questions.q: According to the Philippine Electrical Code, what is the maximum number of convenience outlets allowed on a single 15-ampere branch circuit?
questions.n: Code standards generally limit a 15-amp circuit to 8 outlets to prevent overloading during simultaneous use.

questions.q: Which of the following components is essential for the operation of a fluorescent lamp but is NOT required for an LED lamp?
questions.n: Fluorescent lamps require a ballast to regulate current and a starter for initial ionization; LEDs do not.

questions.q: Which of the following describes the correct wiring size for a standard service drop as per the Philippine Electrical Code (PEC)?
questions.n: The PEC mandates a minimum of 8.0 mm² for service entrance conductors to ensure safety and capacity for the building's total load.

questions.q: What is the primary function of the 'Alternator' within a diesel generator set?
o: To convert mechanical rotation into electrical energy
To regulate the speed of the engine
To burn fuel to create rotational energy
questions.n: The alternator uses electromagnetic induction to transform the engine's mechanical work into AC electricity.

questions.q: When designing a 1-HP Air Conditioning Unit (ACU) circuit, what is the standard recommended wire size and circuit breaker rating?
questions.n: A 3.5 mm² wire paired with a 20A breaker is the standard safety configuration for a 1-HP residential ACU.

questions.q: Which lighting component is used to twist and hold electrical wires together mechanically without the need for soldering?
questions.n: Wire nuts are conical plastic caps with internal threads that secure multiple conductors together safely.

questions.q: In a series circuit, what happens to the remaining lamps if one bulb is removed or burns out?
o: All other lamps will turn off
The remaining lamps stay on at normal brightness
questions.n: In a series circuit, there is only one path for current; if any part of that path is broken, the circuit is open.

questions.q: Which specific device is responsible for receiving signals from fire detectors and activating the building's notification appliances?
questions.n: The FACP is the central hub of an FDAS that processes input from sensors and triggers alarms.

questions.q: What is the standard mounting angle for a spotlight if you want to highlight a painting on a wall without creating harsh glare for the viewer?
questions.n: An angle of 30 degrees from the vertical is the industry standard for museum-quality lighting to minimize glare and shadows.

questions.q: Which of the following companies is a well-known local supplier in the Philippines for security, lighting, and communication systems?
questions.n: Avesco is a prominent Philippine distributor for industrial electrical, security, and broadcast equipment.

questions.q: For a 6-kW multipoint water heater, what is the required circuit breaker ampacity to ensure safe operation?
questions.n: A 30A breaker is the correct size for a 6kW heater, allowing for the ~26A current draw plus a safety margin.

questions.q: In a Business Process Outsourcing (BPO) center, which station in an intercom system has the authority to initiate calls to any other station?
questions.n: The master station is the central hub that controls and directs communication throughout the intercom network.

questions.q: What is the standard color of the 'Neutral' wire in a 230V residential electrical system according to the PEC?
questions.n: The Philippine Electrical Code mandates white or light gray for the neutral conductor.

questions.q: Which type of electrical enclosure is specifically rated for indoor use in environments free of dust and dripping water?
questions.n: NEMA 1 enclosures are general-purpose indoor boxes designed to protect against accidental contact.

questions.q: When control of a light is required from three different locations, how many 4-way switches are needed?
questions.n: Three locations require two 3-way switches at the ends and one 4-way switch in the middle.

questions.q: What component in a generator set provides the 'prime mover' or the source of mechanical energy?
questions.n: The internal combustion engine (diesel or gas) is the prime mover that rotates the alternator shaft.

questions.q: Which of the following lighting fixtures is commonly used for general illumination in commercial ceilings and contains a linear fluorescent or LED tube?
questions.n: Troffers are rectangular lighting fixtures that fit into a dropped ceiling grid.

questions.q: What is the standard 'Service Factor' typically found on electric motor nameplates to indicate their ability to handle brief overloads?
questions.n: A 1.15 Service Factor is common, meaning the motor can handle a 15% overload for short periods.

questions.q: Which electrical switch is designed to automatically disconnect a circuit during an overload or short circuit and can be reset manually?
questions.n: Circuit breakers use a magnetic or thermal mechanism to 'trip' and can be flipped back to the ON position.

questions.q: In lighting design, what term refers to the 'Color Temperature' of a light source, measured in Kelvin (K)?
questions.n: Chromaticity describes the objective quality of a color, including its warmth or coolness.

questions.q: What is the purpose of an 'Emergency Driver' (Figure A in your notes) inside an LED fixture?
o: To change the color of the light to red during an alarm
To protect the fixture from lightning strikes
To provide battery power to the LED during a power failure
To make the light brighter during normal use
questions.n: Emergency drivers contain a battery pack that automatically takes over when main utility power is lost.

questions.q: Which material is used for the outer 'jacket' of a THHN/THWN wire to provide protection against abrasion and moisture?
questions.n: The 'N' in THHN stands for Nylon, which provides a slick, tough outer coating.

questions.q: What is the maximum distance allowed between a manual fire alarm pull station and any point on a floor, according to standard fire safety codes used in the Philippines?
questions.n: Standard fire codes mandate that a pull station must be reachable within 30 meters (approx. 100 feet) from any point to ensure quick manual activation.

questions.q: Which specific device is used to step down the high voltage from a utility line (e.g., 13.8 kV) to the usable building voltage (e.g., 230 V)?
questions.n: Transformers are the primary devices used to transfer electrical energy between circuits through electromagnetic induction while changing voltage.

questions.q: In structured cabling for a BPO, what is the maximum recommended length for a horizontal cable run (typically Cat6) from the telecommunications closet to the work area outlet?
questions.n: The standard TIA/EIA limit for horizontal cabling is 90 meters, allowing an additional 10 meters for patch cords to reach a total of 100 meters.

questions.q: Which of the following describes 'Luminous Flux' and its corresponding SI unit?
o: The total amount of light emitted by a source in all directions; Lumens
Light falling on a surface; Lux
Light intensity in a specific direction; Candela
questions.n: Luminous flux is the time rate of flow of light, measured in lumens (lm).

questions.q: According to the PEC, what is the required clearance for electrical service drop conductors over a residential driveway?
questions.n: The PEC requires a minimum of 3.7 meters (12 feet) clearance for residential driveways to account for vehicle heights.

questions.q: What is the primary function of a 'Ground Fault Circuit Interrupter' (GFCI)?
o: To prevent circuit overloads from too many appliances
To detect small current leaks to ground and trip the circuit to prevent electrocution
To protect equipment from lightning surges
To stabilize voltage during a brownout
questions.n: GFCIs compare the current on the hot and neutral wires; any imbalance (leak) causes an immediate trip to save lives.

questions.q: In a 3-phase power system, which color is most commonly used for 'Phase B' (Line 2) in a standard Philippine commercial installation?
questions.n: Yellow (sometimes Blue) is the standard convention for Phase B in many local 3-phase setups.

questions.q: Which of the following describes an 'Arc Fault Circuit Interrupter' (AFCI)?
o: It provides backup power during a blackout
It detects dangerous electrical sparking (arcing) to prevent fires
It protects against water-related short circuits
It regulates the motor speed in HVAC systems
questions.n: AFCIs identify specific current signatures caused by damaged wires or loose connections that can lead to fire.

questions.q: What is the standard resistance limit for a building's main grounding electrode system to ensure safety?
questions.n: The PEC and NEC generally specify that a single electrode should have a resistance to ground of 25 ohms or less.

questions.q: Which type of detector is most suitable for an electrical room where a fire is likely to produce smoke before a significant rise in temperature?
questions.n: Photoelectric detectors are excellent at sensing larger particles from smoldering fires, common in electrical insulation failures.

questions.q: In lighting, what does the term 'Lumen Maintenance' refer to?
o: The ability to dim the light fixture
The decrease in light output over the life of a lamp
The time it takes for a lamp to reach full brightness
The cost of cleaning the light fixtures
questions.n: Lumen maintenance is the measurement of how much light a lamp produces at a certain point in time compared to its initial output.

questions.q: Which of the following provides the most energy-efficient lighting for a large outdoor parking lot?
questions.n: Modern LEDs provide high efficacy (lumens per watt), long life, and better control for outdoor applications.

questions.q: What is the primary architectural purpose of a 'Parabolic Louver' in a fluorescent or LED troffer?
o: To control glare and direct light more efficiently downward
To keep bugs out of the fixture
To increase the heat dissipation of the fixture
To change the color temperature of the lamp
questions.n: The parabolic shape reflects light into a tight beam, reducing high-angle glare on computer screens.

questions.q: In electrical plans, what does the symbol 'WP' placed next to an outlet signify?
questions.n: WP indicates the outlet must have a protective cover for outdoor or wet location installation.

questions.q: What is the maximum number of degrees of bends allowed in a single run of conduit between pull points (like boxes or fittings)?
questions.n: The PEC/NEC limits a conduit run to 360 degrees (the equivalent of four 90-degree bends) to prevent wire damage during pulling.

questions.q: Which system uses a 'busbar' instead of individual wires to distribute large amounts of current within a building?
questions.n: Busways use solid metal bars (copper or aluminum) in an enclosure for high-ampacity distribution in skyscrapers or factories.

questions.q: What is the minimum height of an electrical wall switch from the finished floor line (FFL) in a standard residential building?
questions.n: 1200 mm (approx. 48 inches) is the standard height for light switches to the center of the box.

questions.q: Which of the following is a 'Direct-Current' (DC) source commonly found in modern green buildings?
questions.n: Solar panels produce DC electricity, which is then converted to AC by an inverter for building use.

questions.q: What is the primary function of a 'Transformer Tap'?
o: To drain oil from the transformer for maintenance
To turn the transformer on and off
To adjust the output voltage to compensate for high or low input voltage
To connect multiple transformers together in parallel
questions.n: Taps allow the turns ratio to be changed slightly to maintain the correct secondary voltage despite utility fluctuations.

questions.q: In the Philippine Electrical Code, what is the 'Ampacity' of a conductor?
o: The length of the wire in a conduit
The maximum current in amperes a conductor can carry continuously without exceeding its temperature rating
The voltage drop across the wire
The resistance of the wire per kilometer
questions.n: Ampacity (Amperage Capacity) is the safe current limit for a wire.

questions.q: What is the maximum number of storeys a building can have before the Philippine Electrical Code (PEC) mandates a second service entrance for emergency power systems?
o: High-rise buildings as defined by the Fire Code
questions.n: While true for fire pumps, the PEC specifically requires separate service for life safety loads in high-occupancy structures to prevent total system failure.

questions.q: Which lighting term refers to the ratio of the luminous flux reaching a specified work plane to the total flux emitted by the lamps in a fixture?
questions.n: The CU measures the efficiency of a lighting system in a specific room environment, accounting for wall reflections and fixture height.

questions.q: In a commercial building, what is the required vertical clearance for an overhead service conductor above a flat roof that is accessible to pedestrians?
questions.n: The PEC requires at least 2.5 meters (8 feet) of clearance to ensure pedestrians cannot easily reach the live wires.

questions.q: Which specific 'Class' of fire alarm system is designed to provide 'supervised' circuits that can detect a wire break or ground fault and signal a trouble alert at the panel?
questions.n: Class A circuits return to the FACP, allowing the system to continue functioning even if a single break occurs in the wiring loop.

o: THHN uses aluminum, while THWN uses copper
THHN is for outdoor use, while THWN is for indoor use
THHN does not have a nylon jacket
THHN has a higher temperature rating in dry locations, while THWN is rated for wet locations

questions.q: Which component in an Escalator system is an electronic safety device that stops the motor if the handrail speed deviates significantly from the step speed?
questions.n: This sensor ensures the handrail moves in sync with the steps to prevent passengers from losing balance.

questions.q: In the context of the PEC, what is the 'Demand Factor' used for when sizing electrical feeders?
o: The ratio of the maximum demand to the total connected load
The total amount of electricity used in a month
The efficiency of a light fixture
The speed at which a generator reaches full voltage
questions.n: Because not all appliances are on at once, the demand factor reduces the calculated load to prevent over-engineering.

questions.q: Which lighting fixture uses a highly polished curved surface to throw light across a large vertical area, like a building facade or a billboard?
questions.n: Wall washers provide uniform vertical illumination and are ideal for architectural highlights.

questions.q: In an office structured cabling system, what is the role of a 'Patch Panel'?
o: To act as a central termination point for horizontal cabling, allowing easy reconnections
To boost the Wi-Fi signal throughout the floor
To provide high-voltage power to the computers
To store backup batteries for the phone system
questions.n: It serves as a static interface between the permanent wall wiring and the active network switches.

questions.n: PIR sensors do not emit energy; they simply detect changes in the heat (infrared) emitted by objects in their field of view.

o: Outlets located within 1.8 meters of a sink
Outlets near the kitchen island wet bar
A dedicated outlet for a refrigerator located behind the appliance

questions.q: According to the PEC, what is the maximum load percentage allowed for a lighting circuit intended for 'continuous use' (operating for 3 hours or more)?
questions.n: Continuous loads must be limited to 80% of the circuit rating to ensure safety and prevent overheating.

questions.q: In a 'Master-Clock' system used in schools or hospitals, what is the primary purpose of the master unit?
o: To tell the exact time to everyone in the building
To serve as a backup generator
To ring the fire alarm bell
questions.n: While true, its technical role is to ensure all clocks in the network are perfectly synchronized.

questions.q: Which type of conduit is the most flexible and often used for the 'final connection' to vibrating equipment like motors or AC units?
questions.n: LFMC has a flexible metal core with a plastic jacket, making it perfect for outdoor motor connections where vibration occurs.

questions.q: Which of the following describes the 'Inverse Square Law' in lighting design?
o: Illuminance is inversely proportional to the square of the distance from the source
The angle of incidence is always equal to the angle of reflection
Illuminance is directly proportional to the distance from the source
Luminous flux increases as the distance increases
questions.n: This fundamental law states that as you double the distance, the light spreads over four times the area, reducing intensity to one-fourth.

questions.q: According to the PEC, what is the required clearance for service-drop conductors over a public street or alley subject to truck traffic?
questions.n: A minimum of 5.5 meters (18 feet) is mandated for public roadways to prevent tall vehicles from striking the lines.

questions.q: Which type of Fire Alarm system circuit return ensures that even with a single 'open' fault, all devices remain operational?
questions.n: Class A circuits loop back to the Fire Alarm Control Panel (FACP), providing an alternate path for signals if the wire breaks.

questions.q: In lighting physics, what is the SI unit for 'Luminous Intensity'?
questions.n: Candela measures the amount of light emitted in a particular direction from a source.

questions.q: What is the primary function of a 'Capacitor Bank' in a large building's electrical room?
o: To step down voltage for electronics
To act as a lightning rod for the main panel
To improve the power factor of the building's system
To store electricity for use during a power outage
questions.n: Capacitor banks counteract the inductive loads of motors and transformers, making the system more efficient and reducing utility penalties.

questions.n: This identifies a transformer cooled by the natural circulation of oil and the natural flow of air over the tank.

questions.q: In a BPO office, what is the purpose of the 'Backbone' cabling (Subsystem 2)?
o: To connect the Telecommunications Room (TR) to the Main Cross-connect (MC)
To provide power to the servers
To act as a physical support for the ceiling pipes
To connect the computers to the desks
questions.n: Backbone cabling provides the high-capacity link between floors or between buildings in a campus.

questions.n: This is the most common AIC (Ampere Interrupting Capacity) rating for residential main breakers.

questions.q: What is the required minimum height of a 'Service Drop' over a public sidewalk as per the PEC?
questions.n: The PEC mandates a 3.1-meter clearance over sidewalks to protect pedestrians.

questions.q: Which acoustic phenomenon occurs when sound waves are reflected multiple times in a room, causing the sound to persist after the source has stopped?
questions.n: Reverberation is the collection of many reflections that prolong the sound in a space.

questions.q: Which specific device is used to measure the total 'Energy' consumed by a building over a period of time?
questions.n: This meter tracks power usage over time, resulting in the 'Kilowatt-Hour' (kWh) units seen on utility bills.

questions.q: What is the primary architectural purpose of a 'Sound Masking' system in an open-plan office?
o: To cancel out all noise so the office is perfectly silent
To amplify the manager's voice during announcements
To play background music for the employees
To increase speech privacy by raising the ambient noise floor
questions.n: By adding a consistent, low-level background sound, distracting conversations become less intelligible and less disruptive.

questions.q: Which wiring method uses a grounded metal enclosure that serves as both the physical protection and the 'Equipment Grounding Conductor'?
questions.n: Because it is metal, properly fitted EMT can serve as the ground path without an extra wire.

questions.q: In the PEC, what is the 'Color Code' for the Grounded (Neutral) conductor?
questions.n: White is the standard identification for the neutral wire in a 230V system.

questions.q: What is the 'Illuminance' on a surface if a light source of 100 candelas is placed 2 meters directly above it?
Which of the following is a 'Direct-Light' source that is often used in retail to create high contrast and drama?
questions.n: Track lights are directional and allow for precise aiming to create pools of light and shadows.

questions.q: In a hospital, 'Life Safety' branch circuits must be automatically restored to power within how many seconds of a utility failure?
questions.n: The code requires critical life safety loads (exit signs, fire alarms) to be powered by the generator within 10 seconds.

questions.q: What is the primary architectural purpose of an 'Escalator Pit'?
o: To house the lower return mechanism and tensioning device
To store spare parts for the escalator
To serve as an emergency exit
questions.n: The pit allows space for the steps to turn around and provides room for the machinery at the base.

questions.q: Which specific sensor is used in an elevator to prevent the doors from closing if a person is standing in the doorway?
questions.n: A multi-beam light curtain detects obstructions across the entire height of the door opening.

questions.q:
In acoustics, what is the 'Absorption Coefficient' of a material that absorbs 
40
%
40% of the sound energy that hits it?
questions.n: The coefficient is expressed as a decimal where 1.0 is total absorption and 0 is total reflection.

questions.q: Which of the following describes 'Luminance'?
o: The amount of light hitting a desk
The brightness of a surface as perceived by the human eye
The total light output of a bulb
The color of the light source
questions.n: Luminance is the light reflected off a surface toward the eye, measured in candelas per square meter.

questions.q: According to the PEC, what is the 'Service Factor' of a motor?
o: The number of hours the motor can run per day
A multiplier that indicates how much the motor can be overloaded without damage
The ratio of peak voltage to RMS voltage
The efficiency of the motor at half load
questions.n: A 1.15 service factor means the motor can handle 15% more than its rated horsepower for short periods.

questions.q: Which type of 'Dry-Type' transformer is most suitable for indoor use where fire safety is the highest priority?
questions.n: The coils are encapsulated in non-flammable epoxy, making them moisture-proof and fire-resistant.

questions.q: What is the function of a 'Traction Machine' in an elevator system?
o: To keep the car perfectly level with the floor
To pump hydraulic oil into the cylinder
To provide the lifting force by using friction between the ropes and the sheave
questions.n: Traction elevators use the 'grip' of the steel cables in the grooves of the drive wheel to move the car.

questions.q: In a BPO, which cable type is most commonly used for 'Vertical' backbone cabling due to its high bandwidth and long-distance capabilities?
questions.n: Fiber uses light pulses and can transmit massive amounts of data across many floors without signal loss.

questions.q: What is the 'Visual Comfort Probability' (VCP)?
o: The likelihood that an LED bulb will last for 5 years
The color accuracy of a light source
The speed at which a person's eyes adjust to the dark
A rating of how likely people are to find a lighting system free of direct glare
questions.n: A VCP of 70 means 70% of people in a specific spot would find the lighting comfortable.

questions.q: According to the PEC, what is the minimum required distance between a 'Grounding Electrode' (Ground Rod) and another grounding electrode?
questions.n: The PEC mandates a 1.9-meter (6-foot) minimum separation between rods.

questions.q: What is the purpose of an 'Automatic Transfer Switch' (ATS)?
o: To automatically switch the building's load from utility power to the generator during an outage
To dim the lights when the sun is bright
To prevent unauthorized access to the IT room
To change the voltage from 230V to 115V
questions.n: The ATS 'senses' the power loss and moves the electrical connection to the emergency source.

questions.q: Which acoustic device is designed to reflect sound in many directions to create a 'diffuse' and rich sound field?
questions.n: Diffusers use uneven surfaces to break up sound reflections, preventing echoes and 'dead spots' in a room.

questions.q: What is the 'Ampacity' adjustment factor for 4-6 current-carrying conductors in a single raceway, according to the PEC?
questions.n: When 4 to 6 wires are bundled, their ampacity is derated to 80% to prevent the conduit from melting.

questions.q: Which specific 'NEMA' enclosure rating is designed for 'Outdoor' use and provides protection against rain, sleet, and external ice formation?
questions.n: NEMA 3R is the standard 'rain-proof' enclosure used for outdoor panelboards and disconnects.

questions.q: In lighting, what is 'Color Rendering Index' (CRI)?
o: The measure of a light source's ability to show colors accurately compared to daylight
The speed at which light travels through a fixture
The color of the actual bulb glass
The temperature of the bulb in degrees Celsius
questions.n: A high CRI (90+) means the light makes colors look vibrant and 'true' rather than washed out.

questions.q: What is the primary function of a 'Circuit Breaker' that is NOT provided by a standard 'Fuse'?
o: It can be reset after it trips
It melts when the current is too high
questions.n: Fuses must be thrown away and replaced after they 'blow', while breakers are simply switched back on.

questions.q: In a hotel, what is the 'STC' (Sound Transmission Class) rating used to measure?
o: The ability of a wall or partition to block airborne sound between rooms
The fire rating of the door
The speed of the elevator car
How much light passes through the windows
questions.n: A higher STC (e.g., 55) means you won't hear your neighbor's TV or conversation.

questions.q: According to the PEC, what is the minimum wire size allowed for a 'Branch Circuit' serving lighting and power in a residence?
questions.n: The PEC allows 2.0 mm² for lighting-only circuits, but 3.5 mm² is standard for most general-purpose outlets.

questions.q: Which component in a 'Centralized AC' system uses electrical power to drive the refrigerant from a low-pressure gas to a high-pressure gas?
questions.n: The compressor is the 'heart' of the system that uses a motor to squeeze the refrigerant.

questions.q: What is 'Efficacy' in lighting?
o: The duration a bulb stays lit after being turned off
The physical size of the fixture
The ratio of light output (Lumens) to power input (Watts)
The cost of the electricity used
questions.n: High efficacy (e.g., 100 lm/W for LED) means the light is very energy-efficient.

questions.q: In an elevator, what is the 'Buffer' used for?
o: To keep the car clean during maintenance
To cushion the impact of the car or counterweight if they travel beyond the lowest floor
To reduce the noise of the doors
To level the car with the floor
questions.n: Buffers are large springs or oil pistons at the bottom of the pit for emergency deceleration.

questions.q: Which fire detector is specifically designed to sense the particles of combustion before a flame is even visible?
questions.n: Smoke detectors sense the 'smoke' particles produced in the early 'smoldering' stages of a fire.

questions.q: What does 'Sabin' measure in the context of room acoustics?
o: The volume of the room in cubic meters
The unit of sound absorption equivalent to one square foot/meter of perfectly absorbing surface
The speed of sound in air
questions.n: It is the 'total' absorption calculated by multiplying the surface area by the material's coefficient.

questions.q: Which of the following is an 'Inductive' load that causes the current to 'lag' behind the voltage?
questions.n: Motors use magnetic coils, which 'resist' changes in current, causing the lag.

questions.q: What is the function of a 'Service Entrance' (Service Head)?
o: To provide a weatherproof connection point between the utility's wires and the building's wiring
To provide a mounting spot for the security camera
questions.n: The service head (or weatherhead) prevents rain from entering the conduit where the wires transition into the building.

questions.q: In lighting, what is the 'Beam Angle' of a spotlight?
o: The angle at which the fixture is mounted

The angle between the two points where the light intensity drops to 
50
%
50% of its maximum
The angle of the shadow cast by an object
The angle at which light reflects off a shiny surface
questions.n: It defines the width of the main 'pool' of light created by the fixture.

questions.q: According to the PEC, what is the 'Minimum Working Space' depth in front of a panelboard with live parts exposed?
questions.n: The PEC mandates a 900 mm (approx. 3 feet) clear working space in front of equipment rated up to 600V.

questions.q: What is the primary technical difference between 'CCTV' and broadcast TV?
o: CCTV is a 'closed' loop intended for a limited number of viewers
CCTV is in black and white only
questions.n: Unlike broadcast signals which go to anyone with an antenna, CCTV signals are private and sent to specific monitors.

questions.q: Which component in a 'Dry-Standpipe' fire system is used by firefighters to pump water into the building?
questions.n: The Siamese connection is located on the building exterior, allowing two fire hoses to pump water into the standpipe.
